inline.s: First, one must arouse the mind of shame. Think of the sages and worthies of old, who were great men like me - why is it that they can be masters for a hundred generations, while I am shattered like a roof tile? ◆ The great Tang man of letters Han Yu, in his essay “On the Origin of Slander,” says: “The noble men of old, in their requirements of themselves, were strict and complete; in their treatment of others they were lenient and forbearing. Strict and complete, and so they did not slacken; lenient and forbearing, and so people were glad to do good. I have heard that among the men of old there was one called Shun; his character as a man was that of a benevolent and righteous man. Seeking what it was that made him Shun, he demanded of himself: “He was a man; I am a man too. Why is it that he could be so, and yet I cannot be so?” Morning and night he pondered this, removing what was not like Shun and attaining what was like Shun.” (Translation: The noble men of old required of themselves what was strict and complete, but required of others what was lenient and forbearing. Strict and complete, and so they did not slacken; lenient and forbearing, and so people were glad to do good.
